records.source: שִׁלְחוּ־כַ֥ר מֹשֵֽׁל־אֶ֖רֶץ מִסֶּ֣לַע מִדְבָּ֑רָה אֶל־הַ֖ר בַּת־צִיּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Send [a] lamb [to the] ruler of [the] land from Sela [toward the] wilderness, to the mountain of [the] daughter of Zion.
pieces: Send the ruler of the land his lamb, from Sela through the wilderness \q to the mountain of Daughter Zion.

L.1: Send a lamb [to] the ruler of the land, from Sela [by way of the] wilderness, \q to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.

R.1: People of Moab, send a lamb as a gift to the ruler of the land. \q Send it from Sela, across the desert, to Mount Zion, where the people of Zion live.

decisions.choice: a lamb for the ruler: tribute sent to the king in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Moab once paid Israel's king tribute in lambs and wool (2 Kings 3:4). Here Moab is told to send it again, to the ruler on Mount Zion, as a sign that it seeks his protection (verses 3-5).

decisions.choice: Sela: "the rock", a place in or toward Edom
decisions.reason: Sela means "rock". A place of this name lay in Edom (2 Kings 14:7); here it may be where Moab's refugees have fled, south of the Wadi of the Poplars (15:7). From there the gift must cross the wilderness to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: send: an appeal to Moab
decisions.reason: The command is plural and addressed to Moab's leaders or people; the speaker is not named. It may be the prophet's advice or the words of Moab's own counselors.

decisions.choice: People of Moab ... as a gift ... where the people of Zion live
decisions.reason: Readable names whom the command is for (m3), says why the lamb is sent (m1), and explains "daughter of Zion" as the people of Zion, as elsewhere in Isaiah.

records.heading: Moab's outcasts seek shelter

records.source: וְהָיָ֥ה כְעוֹף־נוֹדֵ֖ד קֵ֣ן מְשֻׁלָּ֑ח תִּֽהְיֶ֨ינָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת מוֹאָ֔ב מַעְבָּרֹ֖ת לְאַרְנֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And it will be like a bird fluttering, a nest sent away, will be the daughters of Moab [at the] fords of Arnon.
pieces: Like birds darting here and there, like nestlings thrown out, \q the daughters of Moab will be at the crossings of the Arnon.

L.2: And it will be: like a fluttering bird, a nest cast out, \q [so] will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of [the] Arnon.

R.2: The women of Moab will be like frightened birds pushed out of their nest. \q They will wander at the places where people cross the Arnon River.

decisions.choice: the daughters of Moab: the women of Moab
decisions.reason: Most likely the women, fleeing with nowhere to rest. "Daughters" can also mean a land's towns and villages (Numbers 21:25), which would give the same picture of a scattered people.

decisions.choice: a nest sent away: young birds driven from the nest
decisions.reason: "Nest" stands for the young birds in it, scattered and helpless (compare 10:14).

decisions.choice: the fords of the Arnon: crossings on Moab's northern border
decisions.reason: The Arnon runs through a deep gorge into the Dead Sea. Its fords were the crossing points where refugees would gather.

decisions.choice: the places where people cross the Arnon River
decisions.reason: Readable explains "fords" and says the Arnon is a river.

records.source: הָבִ֤יאִי עֵצָה֙ עֲשׂ֣וּ פְלִילָ֔ה שִׁ֧יתִי כַלַּ֛יִל צִלֵּ֖ךְ בְּת֣וֹךְ צָהֳרָ֑יִם סַתְּרִי֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים נֹדֵ֖ד אַל־תְּגַלִּֽי׃
records.gloss: Bring counsel, make [a] decision; make like the night your shade in [the] middle of noon; hide [the] banished; [the] fugitive do not expose.
pieces: Offer counsel; give a ruling. \q Let your shade at midday be as dark as night. \q Shelter the outcasts; do not give away the one who flees.

L.3: Bring counsel, make a decision; \q make your shade like the night in the middle of noon; \q hide the banished; do not expose the fugitive.

R.3: Zion, give us advice. Make a fair decision. \q Protect us like deep shade that is as dark as night in the hot noon sun. \q Hide the people who have run away. \q Do not hand them over to their enemies.

decisions.choice: bring counsel ... hide: Moab's refugees plead with Zion
alternatives: the prophet urges Moab to shelter fugitives
decisions.reason: The commands are spoken to one woman, most naturally Zion (verse 1), by Moab's people asking for shelter; verse 4 continues "my outcasts". Some read them as the prophet's advice to Moab to take in Judah's refugees.

decisions.choice: bring: the scribes' reading, addressed to one woman
decisions.reason: The written text has a plural "bring"; the scribes' reading, followed here, is singular like the other commands. The next command ("make a decision") is plural in the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: shade like night at noon: full protection
decisions.reason: In a hot land shade means shelter and safety (25:4; 32:2). Shade as dark as night at the brightest hour hides the refugees from any pursuer.

decisions.choice: Zion, give us advice
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed and the speakers (m1).

decisions.choice: do not give away
decisions.reason: The verb means to uncover or reveal: do not let pursuers find the fugitive.

records.source: יָג֤וּרוּ בָךְ֙ נִדָּחַ֔י מוֹאָ֛ב הֱוִי־סֵ֥תֶר לָ֖מוֹ מִפְּנֵ֣י שׁוֹדֵ֑ד כִּֽי־אָפֵ֤ס הַמֵּץ֙ כָּ֣לָה שֹׁ֔ד תַּ֥מּוּ רֹמֵ֖ס מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Let them sojourn among you, my banished [ones], Moab; be [a] hiding place for them from [the] face of [the] destroyer. For has come to an end the oppressor, has ceased destruction, have been finished [the] tramplers from the land.
pieces: Let my outcasts from Moab stay among you as guests; \q be a shelter for them from the destroyer. \q For the oppressor will be gone, the ruin will stop, \q and those who trample others will vanish from the land.

L.4: Let my banished ones sojourn among you, Moab; \q be a hiding place for them from the face of the destroyer. \q For the oppressor has come to an end, destruction has ceased, \q the tramplers are gone from the land.

R.4: Let us, the refugees from Moab, live with you. \q Hide us from the enemy who is destroying us. \q One day the cruel oppressor will be gone. The destruction will stop. \q The enemies who crush others will disappear from the land.

decisions.choice: my outcasts, Moab: Moab's refugees speaking of themselves
alternatives: let my outcasts stay with you, Moab
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "my banished ones, Moab". Read with verse 3, Moab's refugees ask Zion to receive them. The ancient Greek translation reads "the outcasts of Moab", with the same sense. An older reading takes "Moab" as addressed: Moab is told to shelter God's outcasts.

decisions.choice: for the oppressor has come to an end: the end of the oppressor is certain
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the completed form, but the end of oppression is still to come; it leads into the promise of a just throne in verse 5.

decisions.choice: the oppressor: one who squeezes or presses
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here; it comes from a root meaning to press or wring out.

decisions.choice: will be gone / will stop
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the future for what is still to come (m2). Literal keeps the completed form.

decisions.choice: us, the refugees from Moab
decisions.reason: Readable states who "my outcasts" are (m1).

records.source: וְהוּכַ֤ן בַּחֶ֨סֶד֙ כִּסֵּ֔א וְיָשַׁ֥ב עָלָ֛יו בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת בְּאֹ֣הֶל דָּוִ֑ד שֹׁפֵ֛ט וְדֹרֵ֥שׁ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּמְהִ֥ר צֶֽדֶק׃
records.gloss: And will be established in loyal love [a] throne, and will sit on it in faithfulness in [the] tent of David [one] judging and seeking justice and swift [in] righteousness.
pieces: A throne will be made secure by loyal love, \q and a ruler will take his seat on it faithfully, in David's tent. \q He will judge, he will search out justice, and he will be quick to act in righteousness.

L.5: And a throne will be established in loyal love, \q and [one] will sit on it in faithfulness in the tent of David, \q judging and seeking justice and swift [in] righteousness.

R.5: Then a king from David's family will rule with faithful love. \q He will sit on his throne and stay faithful. \q He will judge people fairly. He will look for justice and be quick to do what is right.

decisions.choice: a throne in the tent of David: a just king of David's line
decisions.reason: "Tent of David" is David's house and royal line (Amos 9:11). The promise recalls 9:6 and 11:1-5, where a son of David rules in justice and righteousness. The refugees' hope is not in Moab but in this throne.

decisions.choice: loyal love and faithfulness: the covenant virtues of the throne
decisions.reason: The pair of words describes God's own faithfulness (Exodus 34:6) and here the rule of the king who reflects it (Psalm 89:15).

decisions.choice: swift in righteousness: quick to do right
decisions.reason: The word for swift describes a skilled, ready person (Proverbs 22:29; Ezra 7:6). The king does not delay justice.

decisions.choice: a king from David's family ... faithful love ... what is right
decisions.reason: Readable explains "tent of David" as David's family, uses "faithful love" for loyal love, and says "do what is right" for righteousness.

records.source: שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן־מוֹאָ֖ב גֵּ֣א מְאֹ֑ד גַּאֲוָת֧וֹ וּגְאוֹנ֛וֹ וְעֶבְרָת֖וֹ לֹא־כֵ֥ן בַּדָּֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: We have heard [the] pride of Moab, proud very, its haughtiness and its pride and its arrogance; not right its empty boasts.
pieces: We have heard of Moab's pride, proud beyond measure: \q its haughty airs, its pride, its overbearing fury. Its big talk comes to nothing.

L.6: We have heard of the pride of Moab, very proud, \q its haughtiness and its pride and its arrogance; not right [are] its empty boasts.

R.6: We have heard how proud the people of Moab are. \q They are very proud and think they are better than everyone. They are arrogant and full of anger. But their boasting is empty.

decisions.choice: we have heard of the pride of Moab: Moab's pride is well known
decisions.reason: "We" may be Judah, answering Moab's plea, or the prophet with his hearers. Moab's pride is the reason for its fall (25:11; Zephaniah 2:8-10). Jeremiah 48:29-30 repeats this verse almost word for word.

decisions.choice: arrogance, empty boasts: overflowing insolence and idle talk
decisions.reason: The word for arrogance also means overflowing fury. "Not right its empty boasts" means its boasting has no substance and will not come true.

decisions.choice: the people of Moab ... think they are better than everyone
decisions.reason: Readable speaks of Moab's people and explains "haughtiness".

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן יְיֵלִ֥יל מוֹאָ֛ב לְמוֹאָ֖ב כֻּלֹּ֣ה יְיֵלִ֑יל לַאֲשִׁישֵׁ֧י קִיר־חֲרֶ֛שֶׂת תֶּהְגּ֖וּ אַךְ־נְכָאִֽים׃
records.gloss: Therefore will wail Moab for Moab, all of it will wail; for [the] raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth you will moan, only stricken.
pieces: So Moab will wail, Moab for itself, all of it wailing; \q you will moan, crushed and broken, for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth.

L.7: Therefore Moab will wail for Moab, all of it will wail; \q for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth you will moan, utterly stricken.

R.7: So the people of Moab will cry over their land. All of them will cry. \q You will groan in deep sorrow for the sweet raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, which are no more.

decisions.choice: raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth: the city's rich produce, lost
decisions.reason: Raisin cakes were a delicacy and used at feasts (2 Samuel 6:19; Hosea 3:1). Jeremiah 48:31 has "the men of Kir-heres", and some take this word as "foundations". Kir-hareseth is Kir of Moab (15:1; 2 Kings 3:25).

decisions.choice: you will moan, utterly stricken: Moab addressed
decisions.reason: The verb turns to address Moab's people directly. "Only stricken" means wholly struck down.

decisions.choice: sweet ... which are no more
decisions.reason: Readable says why they grieve for raisin cakes: the harvest is lost (verses 8-10).

records.heading: Weeping for the vine of Sibmah

records.source: כִּ֣י שַׁדְמוֹת֩ חֶשְׁבּ֨וֹן אֻמְלָ֜ל גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֗ה בַּעֲלֵ֤י גוֹיִם֙ הָלְמ֣וּ שְׂרוּקֶּ֔יהָ עַד־יַעְזֵ֥ר נָגָ֖עוּ תָּ֣עוּ מִדְבָּ֑ר שְׁלֻ֣חוֹתֶ֔יהָ נִטְּשׁ֖וּ עָ֥בְרוּ יָֽם׃
records.gloss: For [the] terraces of Heshbon languish, [the] vine of Sibmah; [the] lords of [the] nations have struck down its choice branches; to Jazer they reached, they wandered [into the] wilderness; its shoots spread out, they crossed over [the] sea.
pieces: The terraces of Heshbon wilt, and the vine of Sibmah with them; the masters of the nations have beaten down its choicest stems, \q stems that once stretched to Jazer and wandered into the wilderness, \q whose runners spread out and crossed the sea.

L.8: For the terraced fields of Heshbon languish, the vine of Sibmah; the lords of the nations have struck down its choice branches; \q to Jazer they reached; they wandered [into the] wilderness; \q its shoots spread out; they crossed over [the] sea.

R.8: The fields around Heshbon are dying, and the grapevines of Sibmah are dying too. Rulers from other nations have broken down the best vines. \q Those vines once grew as far as the town of Jazer and out into the desert. \q They spread so far that they reached across the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: the lords of the nations have struck down its choice branches
alternatives: its choice wine overcame the lords of the nations
decisions.reason: The line can be read either way round: the foreign rulers struck down Sibmah's vines, or Sibmah's choice wine "struck down" (made drunk) the lords of the nations, a sign of its fame. In the context of ruin the first is taken here.

decisions.choice: Sibmah, Jazer, the sea: Moab's famous vineyards
decisions.reason: Sibmah, near Heshbon, was known for its vines (Numbers 32:38). The vine spreading to Jazer in the north, into the eastern wilderness and across the sea, most likely the Dead Sea, pictures how far its vineyards and fame reached. Jeremiah 48:32 repeats the picture.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Readable names the sea, following m2.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֡ן אֶבְכֶּ֞ה בִּבְכִ֤י יַעְזֵר֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה אֲרַיָּ֨וֶךְ֙ דִּמְעָתִ֔י חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וְאֶלְעָלֵ֑ה כִּ֧י עַל־קֵיצֵ֛ךְ וְעַל־קְצִירֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד נָפָֽל׃
records.gloss: Therefore I weep with [the] weeping of Jazer [for the] vine of Sibmah; I drench you [with] my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, for on your summer fruit and on your harvest [the] shout has fallen.
pieces: That is why I weep along with Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; \q my tears pour over you, Heshbon and Elealeh, \q for the glad shout over your ripe fruit and your harvest has died away.

L.9: Therefore I weep with the weeping of Jazer [for] the vine of Sibmah; \q I drench you [with] my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, \q for on your summer fruit and on your harvest the shout has fallen.

R.9: So I cry for the grapevines of Sibmah, just as the people of Jazer cry. \q Heshbon and Elealeh, my tears soak you. \q People used to shout with joy when they gathered fruit and grain. Now that shouting has stopped.

decisions.choice: the shout has fallen: the harvest cry has ended
alternatives: a war cry has fallen on your summer fruit and harvest
decisions.reason: The word is the shout of the grape treaders (verse 10; Jeremiah 25:30). "Has fallen" most likely means that the joyful shout has stopped. It may instead mean that a shout, the enemy's war cry, has fallen on the harvest (Jeremiah 48:32 has "the destroyer has fallen").

decisions.choice: I weep: the speaker shares Moab's grief
decisions.reason: As in 15:5, the speaker mourns for Moab. In verse 10 God says "I have made the shout cease", so the grief may be the prophet's or God's own (Jeremiah 48:31-36).

decisions.choice: summer fruit and harvest: the late fruit and the grain
decisions.reason: Summer fruit is the ripe fruit of late summer, figs and grapes (Amos 8:1-2); the harvest may be the grain or the vintage.

decisions.choice: People used to shout with joy
decisions.reason: Readable explains the harvest shout (m1).

records.source: וְנֶאֱסַ֨ף שִׂמְחָ֤ה וָגִיל֙ מִן־הַכַּרְמֶ֔ל וּבַכְּרָמִ֥ים לֹֽא־יְרֻנָּ֖ן לֹ֣א יְרֹעָ֑ע יַ֗יִן בַּיְקָבִ֛ים לֹֽא־יִדְרֹ֥ךְ הַדֹּרֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד הִשְׁבַּֽתִּי׃
records.gloss: And are gathered away gladness and joy from the fruitful land, and in the vineyards not is sung, not is shouted; wine in the presses not treads the treader; [the] shout I have made to cease.
pieces: Gladness and delight are gathered up and gone from the garden land. \q In the vineyards there is no singing and no cheering; \q the treader treads no wine in the winepresses. I have silenced the harvest shout.

L.10: And gladness and joy are gathered away from the fruitful land, \q and in the vineyards there is no singing, there is no shouting; \q wine in the presses the treader does not tread; the shout I have made to cease.

R.10: There is no more joy or gladness in the orchards. \q The vineyards are quiet, with no songs and no cheering. \q No one crushes grapes to make wine anymore. I have stopped their happy shouting.

decisions.choice: the fruitful land: orchard and garden country
decisions.reason: The word is the same as the name Carmel, but here it means fertile land planted with fruit trees and vines (10:18; 29:17), not Mount Carmel.

decisions.choice: treading in the presses: making wine
decisions.reason: Grapes were crushed by foot in a pressing floor cut in rock, with singing and shouts (Judges 9:27; Jeremiah 25:30).

decisions.choice: I have made to cease: God speaks
decisions.reason: The "I" who ends the shout is God, who brings the judgment. The verb is in the completed form, as in a vision of what is certain.

decisions.choice: crushes grapes to make wine
decisions.reason: Readable explains treading (m2).

records.source: עַל־כֵּן֙ מֵעַ֣י לְמוֹאָ֔ב כַּכִּנּ֖וֹר יֶֽהֱמ֑וּ וְקִרְבִּ֖י לְקִ֥יר חָֽרֶשׂ׃
records.gloss: Therefore my inward parts for Moab like [a] harp sound, and my inner being for Kir-heres.
pieces: So deep within me I moan for Moab like a plucked lyre, \q and my inmost being moans for Kir-heres.

L.11: Therefore my inward parts sound like a lyre for Moab, \q and my inner being for Kir-heres.

R.11: My heart aches for Moab. It makes a sad sound, like the music of a harp. \q Deep inside I mourn for Kir-heres.

decisions.choice: my inward parts sound like a lyre: deep grief
decisions.reason: The inward parts are the seat of feeling. Their sound is compared to the low, throbbing note of a stringed lyre (compare Jeremiah 48:36, which uses flutes).

decisions.choice: Kir-heres: Kir-hareseth
decisions.reason: A shorter form of the name in verse 7, Moab's capital (15:1); Jeremiah 48:31, 36 has the same form.

decisions.choice: lyre
decisions.reason: The instrument was a small stringed lyre; Readable says "harp", the more familiar word.

decisions.choice: moans
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats the verb in the second line, which the Hebrew leaves understood.

records.source: וְהָיָ֧ה כִֽי־נִרְאָ֛ה כִּֽי־נִלְאָ֥ה מוֹאָ֖ב עַל־הַבָּמָ֑ה וּבָ֧א אֶל־מִקְדָּשׁ֛וֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל וְלֹ֥א יוּכָֽל׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when it appears, when has wearied itself Moab on the high place and comes to its sanctuary to pray, and not it will prevail.
pieces: Moab will come before its god and tire itself out at the high place; \q it will go into its sanctuary to pray, and it will accomplish nothing.

L.12: And it will be, when Moab appears, when it wearies itself on the high place \q and comes to its sanctuary to pray, it will not prevail.

R.12: The people of Moab will go to their hilltop altars and worship until they are worn out. \q They will go into their temple to pray. But it will do them no good.

decisions.choice: appears: comes before a god in worship
decisions.reason: The verb "appear" is used of coming before God at a shrine (1:12; Exodus 23:15). Moab's god was Chemosh (Numbers 21:29; 1 Kings 11:7).

decisions.choice: it will not prevail: its prayers gain nothing
decisions.reason: Moab's weeping at the high place (15:2) and its prayers in its sanctuary cannot turn back the disaster. The repeated "when" may also be a doubled emphasis, "even when".

decisions.choice: before its god
decisions.reason: Balanced says before whom Moab appears (m1).

records.source: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־מוֹאָ֖ב מֵאָֽז׃
records.gloss: This [is] the word which spoke Yahweh concerning Moab from then.
pieces: Such was the word {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke about Moab in earlier days.

L.13: This [is] the word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke concerning Moab from of old.

R.13: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said about Moab long ago.

decisions.choice: from then: in the past, earlier
decisions.reason: The oracle of 15:1-16:12 is called a word spoken before; verse 14 adds a new word for "now". It may have been given earlier in Isaiah's ministry, or be an older word about Moab taken up here; Jeremiah 48 uses much of it again.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בְּשָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ כִּשְׁנֵ֣י שָׂכִ֔יר וְנִקְלָה֙ כְּב֣וֹד מוֹאָ֔ב בְּכֹ֖ל הֶהָמ֣וֹן הָרָ֑ב וּשְׁאָ֥ר מְעַ֛ט מִזְעָ֖ר ל֥וֹא כַבִּֽיר׃ס
records.gloss: And now has spoken Yahweh, saying, in three years like [the] years of [a] hired worker, and will be lightly esteemed the glory of Moab with all the multitude the great, and [the] remnant [will be] little, few, not mighty.
pieces: But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: Within three years, counted as a hired worker counts them, the glory of Moab with all its great throng will be treated as nothing, and those left over will be a handful, without strength.

L.14: And now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken, saying: Within three years, like the years of a hired worker, the glory of Moab will be held in contempt, with all [its] great multitude, and the remnant [will be] small, few, not mighty.

R.14: But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: In exactly three years, Moab's glory will be gone. All its crowds of people will be looked down on. Only a few weak people will be left.

decisions.choice: like the years of a hired worker: exactly counted
decisions.reason: A hired man works for a fixed term and counts the days; the time will be no longer than stated (21:16).

decisions.choice: the glory of Moab will be held in contempt: its honor made light
decisions.reason: "Glory" is from the root "heavy"; it will become "light", a play on words. The glory is Moab's wealth, power and many people.

decisions.choice: the remnant small, few, not mighty: a weak handful left
decisions.reason: Moab is not wholly wiped out, but its survivors will be few and weak.

decisions.choice: In exactly three years ... will be gone
decisions.reason: Readable explains "like the years of a hired worker" (m1) and says plainly what contempt for Moab's glory means.
